kevin (customer): Hey team, urgent: our streaming responses sometimes end with an incomplete JSON blob. No final finish_reason and no trailing [DONE] event. Seen ~12 times in last 4 hours. Request id: req_48b7f2b0. Example of last bytes our client got:

kevin (customer): ...\n

{"id":"resp_abc123","object":"text_completion","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"...the final sentence ends he"}}

// stream stops here, client hits EOF, JSON invalid (array/object not closed)

kevin (customer): Repro steps from our production box:

curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=longgen"

kevin (customer): We tried reconnecting but don't see resumable tokens from your side, so we have to restart generation which loses context. Any guidance?

maya (support): Thanks Kevin, this is actionable. Can you paste your reverse-proxy logs around req_48b7f2b0 and tell us what sits in front of your app (NGINX, ALB, Cloud Load Balancer, CloudFront)?

kevin (customer): We're behind an internal nginx reverse proxy + AWS ALB. Nginx error (truncated):

2026/06/12 14:02:30 [error] 1234#0: *789 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.5, server: -, request: "GET /v1/streams?model=longgen HTTP/1.1", upstream: "https://upstream-internal:8443/v1/streams?model=longgen", host: "api.redwood.example"

kevin (customer): ALB logs around the same time show TargetResponseTime ~78.45 and then connection_status="HIT" (we'll upload full logs).

irina (eng): Two likely root causes: 1) backend process closed/crashed before final flush, or 2) intermediate proxy/ALB cut the TCP due to idle/timeout. The nginx error you pasted usually indicates the proxy detected the upstream close. We need server-side correlation. Maya, can you pull service logs for req_48b7f2b0 (trace id) and stream write counters? We log both final payload and a flush_ack.

support-bot: log_event: trace_id=resp-trace-48b7f2b0, rpc=session-22, worker=gw-07, model=longgen, start=2026-06-12T14:01:22Z
support-bot: stream_event: wrote_chunk size=32768 seq=124
support-bot: stream_event: wrote_chunk size=8192 seq=125
support-bot: stream_event: wrote_chunk size=4096 seq=126
support-bot: final_event: wrote_chunk size=512 seq=127 finish_payload_present=true
support-bot: flush_ack: not_received before connection_close
support-bot: connection_closed_by_peer at 2026-06-12T14:02:30Z

irina (eng): Our side shows we wrote the final chunk and it contained the finish payload on disk/network stack, but we never got a flush ACK before the TCP connection closed. That pattern points to an intermediate timeout dropping the connection mid-stream. Common culprits: ALB idle timeout (often 60s), nginx proxy_read_timeout (defaults vary), or other LBs with 60s cutoff.

maya (support): Kevin, can you try bypassing nginx and curl the ALB/public endpoint directly for a quick check? Also try curl with `--no-buffer` and add header `Connection: keep-alive`. If direct to ALB succeeds but via nginx fails, it narrows to your proxy.

kevin (customer): Quick test: direct to ALB completed successfully once. Through nginx it failed. Our nginx conf snippet: 

```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
proxy_send_timeout 60s;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
```

kevin (customer): Changing `proxy_read_timeout` to 180s on a test box fixed the immediate repro. We can't change production ALB timeout quickly though.

irina (eng): That explains it. Short term: bump reverse proxy timeouts. Longer term we should emit periodic keepalive SSE comments (or small progress events) every ~8-10s for long-running streams so proxies see activity and don't classify connection as idle. Also, add a last-chunk sentinel that is easy for clients to detect even if JSON gets cut (e.g., an explicit final `data: {"meta":{"finish_reason":"stop"}}` event). We should also attempt linger/flush to increase odds the final bytes reach the TCP layer.

maya (support): Proposed hotfix steps: 1) server: emit keepalive events every 8s for streaming responses expected >30s, 2) server: include an explicit final sentinel event with finish_reason, 3) infra: document recommended proxy/LB timeouts and examples for nginx/ALB, 4) add metrics/obs for missing flush_ack so we can detect the pattern.

kevin (customer): One more client-side note: node-fetch and some fetch polyfills will throw as soon as a parse error occurs and don't attempt reconnects. Any suggested defensive client patterns?

irina (eng): Client-side recommendations: use streaming JSON parsers (evented parser) to handle partial chunks gracefully, treat missing finish_reason as retryable for idempotent flows, implement a short delay on EOF to allow for late bytes (if transport might still deliver), or use a resumable protocol (we don't currently surface resumable tokens for generation). We'll document patterns and provide example snippets.

maya (support): Creating tracking ticket S-6789, assigned to eng (irina). Action items:
- Support: collect all affected req ids and attach ALB/nginx logs (Kevin)
- Eng: implement keepalive + final sentinel and add regression test simulating proxy cutoff (irina)
- Infra: add recommended proxy timeout docs + quickstart guidance (maya + infra)
- Support: monitor for recurrence and escalate if keepalive doesn't resolve

kevin (customer): Thanks, increasing nginx timeouts is a good short-term workaround for us. We'll also add a tolerant streaming JSON parser client-side until the sentinel is live. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

irina (eng): For the eng ticket, planned SSE pseudo-payloads: 

```
: keepalive

// periodic progress event (every ~8s)
data: {"type":"progress","generated_tokens":1234}

// final sentinel
data: {"meta":{"finish_reason":"stop"}}
```

irina (eng): We'll also add a regression that starts a 90s generation and simulates an nginx/ALB idle cut to confirm sentinel delivery and client visibility of finish_reason.

maya (support): I'm leaving this thread open until Kevin confirms production behavior. S-6789 will be updated with deploy progress.

kevin (customer): Copy that. Will report back after we've validated production. Thanks again.
